items.title: 67256_Paul L. Howard oral history interview
items.q: one of the main persons that I met at that time was Mr. Markham

ctx.x: you couldn't always play what you wanted to play. You couldn't always do it.

So my uncle was directing the choir at 8th and San Julian. So I had to skip to the Sunday morning we went to church, and the first thing he did was make me grab hold of my -- the first thing he did was get me to grab -- to get my instruments out and come and go to church and play in the choir, as he was the choir director. And the director of this choir, maybe somebody in Los Angeles might hear this and may know this -- the director of the choir was my uncle. His name was Walter V. Howard, my father's brother.…

But anyhow, I had a very nice reception here at church. I got up and played a solo, and I want to try to think of the name, if these gentlemen will allow me the time to think of the name of the solo I played. And I had -- it was a book -- the book was put out by -- oh, boy -- had all the classics in it. It's a funny thing. Shut it off a minute, Red.
